clue.text: Editing ad, rethink location of hopeless shot?

indicators.note: editing reworks material into a new form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An advertising team, revising a campaign, rethinks where to place a doomed photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: A wild guess is a shot in the dark, so the darkness is where such a hopeless shot lands; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a shot in the dark' names a guess with little chance, so being without light is where such a shot is placed.

clue.text: South American in London area leaving 'as a precaution'

indicators.note: the London area leaving the phrase means its letters go out of it

parts.note: 'in case' means as a precaution
SE is the south-east postal district of London

explanation.surface: A traveller from South America in London is told to leave just to be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Take SE out of IN CASE to leave INCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the native people of the Andes whose empire was centred on Peru, so one is a South American.

clue.text: Melt what?

parts.note: surface reading: a demand to make something liquefy
setter's reading: the answer, read as an instruction, takes a four-letter word and shakes it out to make the word 'what'

explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, its first word mixed up ('out') gives WHAT, while the whole phrase means melt.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw out is to unfreeze, so frozen food or ice softening and turning liquid is melting.

clue.text: Former partner abandoned pet, evil 'xxxx'!

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the following letters run riot

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone's ex walked out on the family pet, which prompts an evil four-letter outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: The row of x's stands for a censored swear word, as printed transcripts mark one 'expletive deleted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-letter word blanked out with x's is a swear word, and an expletive is an oath or obscenity.

clue.text: Intermission in war film stops Erica fidgeting

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so one word sits inside the other
someone fidgeting keeps shifting about, so the name's letters move

parts.note: letters to rearrange
a film is a thin layer or haze, like mist

explanation.surface: During the interval of a war movie, a restless Erica gets the film halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intermission' and 'film' suggest a cinema, but the definition is a pause in fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, an agreed halt to hostilities, so it is a break in the fighting.

clue.text: King tees off in hallowed Scottish venues

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to tee someone off is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A monarch drives off the first tee at Scotland's revered golf courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tees off' and 'Scottish venues' paint golf at St Andrews; the hallowed venues are churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirk is the Scots word for a church, so kirks are consecrated places of worship north of the border.

clue.text: Area of France that's near Luxembourg and Germany

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A geography question: which region of France borders Luxembourg and Germany?
explanation.walkthrough: The countries reduce to the letters on car badges, and 'near' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A field is a sphere or area, of study or activity as well as of land.

clue.text: Belief in those running football damaged top to bottom

indicators.note: in a down light the top letter is sent to the foot of the word

parts.note: the FA (Football Association) governs English football
hit as in struck or harmed

explanation.surface: Fans' trust in football's governing body has been badly hurt, from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT has its first letter moved to the end, giving ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is trust or religious conviction, a synonym for belief.

clue.text: Sanctimonious chap probing both sides of emotive affair

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so the man goes in
both sides of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: its first and last letters
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
sod is British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A self-righteous man digs into a heated, emotional business.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi is old school slang for pious, and sod is a British slang word for a fellow; 'both sides of' means only the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is an incident or occurrence, as is an affair in the sense of a matter or event.

clue.text: Day perhaps to see to teacher's retirement

parts.note: to do something is to see to it

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the title is read back up the light

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir

explanation.surface: A day might be set aside to arrange a schoolmaster's leaving do.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Day was the American singer and film star, so 'Day' is a surname, signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress Doris Day is one bearer of the surname Day, so the first name is an example.

clue.text: 50% off sparkling wines — that's a winner!

indicators.note: half the word is taken away, leaving only the front five letters

parts.note: the best-known sparkling wines

explanation.surface: A shop advert: half price on fizz, a real winner of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten-letter plural loses its back five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is short for champion, someone who has won a title or contest.

clue.text: It's cold west of Montana, wetter east of Montana

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for Montana
rainier means wetter, of weather

explanation.surface: A weather report: chilly in the west of Montana, rainy in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'east of' means placed after. Mount Rainier is a snow-capped volcano in Washington state, west of Montana.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Rainier is a glaciated peak in Washington, a cold summit that lies to the west of the state of Montana.

clue.text: Fans of one-day cricket format?

parts.note: a one-day international lasts fifty overs per side; L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A question about supporters of limited-overs cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: One-day cricket is a fifty-over game; the question mark admits the stretch of turning fifty into L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers of something are its keen devotees or enthusiasts, just as fans are.

clue.text: Coaches groups of 25?

explanation.surface: Coaches as buses carrying school parties of twenty-five children.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is a cross-reference to 25 across, SALMON, and fish swim in schools; class sizes of 25 are the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train them, and a school is also a shoal of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Water lover going back in: swimming or fishing?

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read right to left
the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, crossing its word gaps

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of swimming, the word or and the start of fishing

explanation.walkthrough: Read swimminG OR Fishing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is an amphibian that lives in and around ponds, so it is fond of water.

clue.text: Selling wingless nuts and bolts, possibly to drill association

indicators.note: a drill bores into material, so one piece goes into the other
a thing without wings loses its two sides, so the outer letters go

explanation.definitionFit: Retailing is selling goods to the public, so it is a form of selling.

clue.text: GI less sad after training manoeuvres on mountain

indicators.note: training reshapes recruits, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An American soldier is cheered up by exercises in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: A GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissade is a controlled slide down a snow slope on the feet, a technique used by climbers descending.

clue.text: Ancient implement, hoe, revamped with bits of duck tape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bits of the words means just a small piece of each, their first letters

parts.note: the initial letter of each word

explanation.surface: An old garden hoe has been patched up with gaffer tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' looks like a noun, a tool; it is a verb, and the answer is the Biblical form of 'does'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeth is the old form of 'does', and to implement something is to do or carry it out.

clue.text: Crumpled blouse found during party for couples

indicators.note: found during the party means sitting within it

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: a crumpled garment is creased out of shape, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to rearrange

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' wants to be a social do, but it is a political party here.
explanation.definitionFit: To double up is to pair off or share, as when people couple up two to a room.

clue.text: Bulge throbbing softly

parts.note: a hum is a steady throbbing sound
p is the musical notation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A swelling that pulses gently.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the music direction piano, meaning softly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hump is a rounded lump or protuberance, as a bulge is.

clue.text: I caught detached iceberg turning back diver

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.walkthrough: 'Diver' suggests a person; it is a diving water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebes are water birds that dive under the surface to catch fish, so a grebe is a diver.

clue.text: Thrilling night out: husband wasted after knocking back booze

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
knocking back a drink is downing it, but here back means the word runs backwards
the husband is wasted, thrown away, so his letter goes

parts.note: ale is beer, a kind of booze
taken as written
h is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A big night out ends with the husband drunk after downing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' and 'knocking back' read as drunkenness, but they are instructions: a removal and a turnaround.

clue.text: Seeking enjoyment in grand old city: 'Coot's Touring Society'

clue.text: Vow one's kept in university, finding love

clue.text: Important question and answer session, finally, with corporation

parts.note: its final letter

clue.text: Worried about fabricated denial? The opposite is conveyed

ate as in 'what's eating you', worried

clue.text: You must record this match?

clue.text: Show contempt for Michelle Mone, maybe calling out 'get lost!'
